scientific_claim: Chemical filtering can enrich T relative to U through differential hydrolysis stability in dark hydrothermal-vent conditions. UV is negligible in this environment (zero-UV control differs by <2%). The model does not demonstrate Darwinian evolution. The CSI decomposes multiplicatively as CSI = real T-pref enrichment * pool-drift factor; the drift factor is a DERIVED RESIDUAL (drift = CSI / real), not an independently simulated mechanism. CSI is normalized by the INITIAL Miller-Orgel pool T-fraction (0.0661), not by the influx T-fraction (0.2727); csi_vs_influx and drift_independent are recorded as convention-free diagnostics. The stability ratio k_U/k_T is an Arrhenius extrapolation, not a measurement; see the Ea_T sweep. The decisive_control_sweep tests whether the enrichment survives forcing k_U == k_T in (a) the polymer only, (b) the free pool only, and (c) both. The legacy UV module encodes T as LESS photoreactive than U, the OPPOSITE of the measured direction in Khosh Abady et al. (PNAS 2026); use uv_damage_mode='lesion_two_state' for the PNAS-informed two-state lesion model.

model_abstractions.homopolymer: Every 'DNA molecule' is a homopolymer of 100 residues of one base; no sequence, no base pairing, no complementary strand; 'dsDNA' is a label only.
model_abstractions.csi_normalization: CSI = final DNA T-fraction / INITIAL-pool T-fraction (0.0661); influx T-fraction is 0.2727.
model_abstractions.drift_is_residual: pool_drift_factor = CSI / real by definition; see drift_independent for an independent diagnostic.
model_abstractions.uv_selectivity: legacy_irreversible mode: T cross-section 0.28x U (opposite of PNAS 2026). lesion_two_state mode: T hit rate 2.7x U (PNAS-informed), lesions split into reversible CPDs and lethal (6-4).
model_abstractions.free_monomer_hydrolysis: Free U/T hydrolysis rate = polymer rate * FREE_HYDRO_SCALE (assumed, default 1.0); placeholder for measured free-nucleotide kinetics.
model_abstractions.decomposed_destruction_channels: polymer hydrolysis and free-monomer hydrolysis are independently equalizable; equal_polymer_only and equal_free_only isolate the two channels; equal_degradation equalizes both.

known_limitations: Homopolymer abstraction: results describe populations of single-base 100-mers, not copolymeric genetic molecules.
The k_U/k_T ~ 357x stability ratio is inherited almost entirely from the assumed 25 C reference-rate ratio (1.3e-10 / 1.1e-13 ~ 1182x) plus assumed Ea values; it is an input, not an output.
FREE_HYDRO_SCALE, CPD fractions, and PHOTOREVERSION_RATE are assumed placeholders; sweeps bound but do not measure their influence.
CSI magnitude depends on pool-composition conventions (initial pool vs influx); see the equal_pools control.
No Darwinian evolution: no replication with heredity or selection on fidelity.

optimization_results.stability_ratio_label: extrapolated (25 C refs -> 90 C; Ea_T assumed 32 kcal/mol; see ea_T_sweep for uncertainty)

decisive_control_sweep.decision_rule: Claim 'free-pool hydrolysis drives enrichment' is SUPPORTED if equal_polymer_only CSI ~ baseline CSI AND equal_free_only CSI ~ equal_degradation CSI (both within 95% CI). REFUTED if equal_polymer_only CSI drops substantially toward 1 OR equal_free_only CSI stays near baseline. MIXED otherwise.
